packs.title: Coast, Gardens and Stories
packs.promise: Explore Santa Cruz through separate coast, garden, history and greenbelt outings.

q.s: Connect a historic ranch feature to a coastal landscape.
st: Identify one credited ranch building or interpretation point on the open public route.
From a safe mapped path, record one coastal terrace or bluff feature visible nearby.
Write a paired note distinguishing the documented ranch use from your direct landscape observation.

q.s: Link a credited object to the habitat described beside it.
st: Choose one credited natural-history specimen or object in a current exhibit or the museum's official online material.
Record what the museum actually identifies and the habitat or process it connects to that object.
Write one observation and one sourced fact, then mark any question the display does not answer.

q.s: Compare two credited works or local-history sources in context.
st: Choose two credited works or historical sources currently accessible at the MAH or on its official site.
Record each maker or source institution and one fact actually supplied by its label.
Create a short comparison of how the two sources frame Santa Cruz, separating their claims from your own response.

packs.title: West Cliff to Beach
packs.promise: Walk Santa Cruz's headland, wetland and beachfront in connected outings.

q.s: Compare two habitat cues on an open coastal loop.
st: Choose a short open section of the park's public multi-use trail.
Record one grassland or tree-edge cue and one bay-facing cue from safe footing.
Write a comparison of the two habitat edges without approaching animals or leaving the path.

q.s: Read two habitat layers from a public boardwalk.
st: Enter from an open public access point and read one interpretive sign or city source.
From the boardwalk, identify two visible layers such as open water, marsh plants or upland path without guessing a species.
Draw a two-layer section showing how visitors pass through without entering the sensitive wetland.

q.s: Map two public recreation zones from safe dry land.
st: From a safe public sidewalk or dry beach edge, identify two distinct recreation zones, such as court area and shore access.
Use the city's beach source to locate Main Beach between the Wharf and San Lorenzo River mouth.
Make a simple orientation map showing how the two zones coexist without assigning activities to individual people.
